questions.question:
Study the following pie-chart carefully, which shows a state government's expenditure (% allocation) on various sectors during the year 2019.

If ₹27 million were spent on transport in 2019, what would have been the total expenses (in million) of the given state government in that year considering mentioned sectors only?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d8ea7a7585bb066f7977cbaca86d9e3b047a1f9cdd7f63c77b7e31cf63e9423d.png]
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Spent on transport in 2019 = Rs 27 million

Expenses share of transport = 18%

Expenses share of agriculture = 30%

Expenses share of health = 15%

Expenses share of irrigation = 25%

Expenses share of dairy = 12%

**Concept Used:**

Total composition of each sector = Percentage Expenses × Amount in one percent

**Calculation:**

⇒ 18% of transport expenses contain = Rs 27 million = Rs 27,000,000

⇒ 1% of the expenses include = (27000000)/(18)=1,500,000

⇒ Now, Expenses share of agriculture = 30 times 1500000=45,000,000

⇒ Expenses share of health = 15×1500000=22,500,000

⇒ Expenses share of irrigation = 25×1500000=37,500,000

⇒ Expenses share of dairy = 1500000×12=18,000,000

⇒ Total Expenses of all sectors = 27,000,000 + 45,000,000 + 22,500,000 + 37,500,000 + 18,000,000

⇒ Total Expenses of all sectors = Rs 150,000,000

**Hence, the total expenses (in million) of the given sectors in the state government is 150 million.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__** From the pie chart,

Expense on transport = 18%

18% = 27 M

Then total expense = 100% = (27/18) * 100 = **150 M**

Cost on Promotion = 10% of T

Cost on Paper = 25% of T

The following pie chart shows the spending of a country on tourism in various districts during a particular year. Total spending of the country = ₹15,62,000. Study the pie chart and answer the following question.

The amount spent on districts D and E exceeds that on district A and F by (in ₹):
questions.solution:
**Concept Used:**

Percentage of money spent = Percentage of district × Total spend of the country

**Calculation: **

⇒ Percentage of money spent on districts D & E = 16 + 18 = 34 %

⇒ Percentage of money spent on districts A & F = 12 + 12 = 24 %

⇒ Thus, money spent on districts D & E exceeds that on E & F by 34 – 24 = 10%

⇒ 10 % of Total Spend = (10)/(100) times 1562000 = Rs. 1,56,200

**Hence, the money spent on districts D & E exceeds that on E & F by Rs. 1,56,200**

questions.solution:

100% represents Total number of books

 State. B = 24% and State C = 18%

State D = 25% and State E= 20%

**Hence, the difference is 75.**

Find the difference between the number of students who appeared for the exam in sections A and B
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Total appeared students = 1800

Angle for section A = 42°

Angle for section B = 50°

**Formula used:**

Number of students in a section = (Angle / 360°) × Total students

**Calculations:**

Number of students in section A = (42 / 360) × 1800 = 210

Number of students in section B = (50 / 360) × 1800 = 250

Difference = 250 - 210 = 40

**∴ The difference between the number of students who appeared for the exam in sections A and B is 40.**

The expenditure on education is greater than housing = 75° – 60°.

⇒ 15°

According to the given,

⇒ 1° = 2700/15 

⇒ Rs. 180

The total expenditure on food and clothing = 125° + 18° 

⇒ 143°

Then, 1° = Rs. 180

⇒ 143° = 180× 143

⇒ Rs. 25,740
